argument_summary: The strongest admissible defense is narrow. Certification is supportable as a launch-readiness decision because aggregate readiness passed by 2.4 percentage points and the launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, with public governance guidance supporting documented limitations and post-deployment measurement and monitoring. But the same admissible record weakens any clean defense of certification without a material weakness disclosure: the municipal permitting assistant misses target by 1.3 percentage points, it is named in two city pilot commitments, legal review is still open, and there is no admissible evidence of either disclosure or approved risk acceptance. The audit packet should therefore defend certification only in that limited form and record the disclosure weakness explicitly rather than escalate beyond the locked certification decision.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is offered as a substitute for policy satisfaction. The practical reason to avoid further escalation is narrower: the existing admissible record is enough to document why certification was chosen as a readiness decision while also preserving the unresolved disclosure issue as a recorded caveat for monitoring and follow-up.
claims_about_policy: Aggregate readiness evidence and public governance guidance can support certification process quality, but they do not by themselves satisfy the internal release-policy condition for a material limitation in a named launch use case. On the present admissible record, the affected segment appears material under the stated policy because it is named in customer commitments and legal review is pending. There is no admissible evidence that the limitation was disclosed before launch or covered by approved risk acceptance. The supportable policy position is therefore not clean compliance on omission of disclosure, but a caveated certification record that explicitly preserves the unresolved materiality and disclosure issue.
concessions: The municipal permitting assistant segment misses its target by 1.3 percentage points.
That segment is named in two city pilot commitments, which makes the limitation facially material under the stated policy.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance covering this limitation before launch.
There is no admissible evidence that the limitation was disclosed before launch.
The open legal ticket means the record does not contain a resolved disclosure determination.
